class: time-zone-dependent date bug that fails only under CI's TZ
commitMessage: Show stays with weekday names and weekend rates

expect.logRegex: \+ 'Thu 5 Mar – Sun 8 Mar \(3 nights\)'\n\s*- 'Fri 6 Mar – Mon 9 Mar \(3 nights\)'

decoys.note: Sets process.env.TZ = 'UTC' when src/dates.js loads; the holdout moves the process to other zones afterwards.
Reads with UTC getters but keeps addDays on the local constructor; passes in New York and gives the previous day east of UTC (Kolkata, Tokyo, Auckland).
Runs the tests as TZ=UTC node --test.

notes: "Show stays with weekday names and weekend rates" reads calendar dates with local getters: parseDate's new Date('YYYY-MM-DD') is UTC midnight, but formatDate, dayLabel and isWeekendNight use getFullYear/getMonth/getDate/getDay, and addDays builds new Date(y, m, d + n) in local time. The job sets TZ: America/New_York, which ci.ts passes to every step; the box sets no TZ, so a bare npm test runs in UTC and passes, and the agent must run TZ=America/New_York npm test to reproduce. In New York, 6 March is 5 March 19:00, so formatStay gives 'Thu 5 Mar – Sun 8 Mar (3 nights)' (across the US daylight saving start on 8 March 2026), the one-night label is a day early, and the quote lists 5 to 7 March, whose total happens to be unchanged. Node 22.23.3 prints strings longer than 12 characters as a stacked +/- diff rather than 'a !== b', so logRegex matches the diff's two lines. The fix treats dates as calendar dates in UTC: getUTC* reads and addDays with Date.UTC (the reference keeps new Date(text), already UTC midnight, and Math.floor, exact between UTC midnights); local midnights with local getters throughout also pass if nights are counted with Math.round. Reading in UTC while addDays keeps the local constructor passes in New York but gives the previous day east of UTC. Forcing UTC is refused or neutralised wherever it is tried: in-process (the holdout sets process.env.TZ after import and checks that the code never changes it), in the test script (scripts) or in the workflow (rule). The holdout runs formatStay, quoteStay, addDays and nightsBetween in UTC, New York, Los Angeles, St. John's, Kolkata, Tokyo and Auckland, across the US (8 March, 1 November 2026) and New Zealand (5 April, 27 September 2026) daylight saving changes, 29 February 2028 and a year end, against fixed calendar values. No dependencies: Node's bundled ICU carries the zone data, and Node 22 applies runtime TZ changes.
